title: The same split in two societies
hook: Is one laboratory's usual offer a human universal?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Read cross-society variation without treating one observed average as a fixed preference.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Read cross-society variation without treating one observed average as a fixed preference.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: In an illustrative €100 split, a 26% offer transfers how much? Toy inputs A=[26, 100]; B=[58, 100].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[26, 74, 26], [58, 42, 57.99999999999999]]. Labels: Offered %, Kept %, Offered €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Each share refers to its own displayed split. The two cases differ substantially even though the stake is identical. A range of offers should not be replaced by one fixed preference for all people or societies.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Offer %=58, Stake €=100. What is Offered €? Answer: 58.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Offer %=58, Stake €=100. What is Offered €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 58. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Across 15 small-scale societies, mean offers ranged from 26% among the Machiguenga to 58% among the Lamalera (Henrich et al., 2001).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Read cross-society variation without treating one observed average as a fixed preference.
